title: Legal redlines scratchpad - Harper Evans
content:
Quick scratchpad for redlines and negotiation talking points

Context: customer is a mid-market SaaS (Product Analytics). Received initial redline — focus areas below. Notes are rough; share with Legal lead (Maya) before client call.

Top-line risk areas to watch
- Data use / training: customer insists "no training" on their data. Need explicit clause: vendor will not use customer data to train models or improve model weights. Proposed fallback: allow aggregate/anonymous telemetry for reliability only with opt-out.
- Data residency & encryption: customer requires EU residency and KMS-managed keys. Check Private deployment offering and Dedicated commitment. Confirm HSM/KMS options and audit logs availability.
- Confidentiality: extend period to 5 years post-termination for sensitive PII. Add carve-outs for aggregated non-identifying metrics.
- Liability cap: customer wants unlimited liability for data breaches. Our standard = fees x 12 months. Escalation point: if high-risk regulated data, recommend separate carveout + cyber-insurance requirement.
- Indemnity: remove third-party IP indemnity for model outputs? Customer requests broad IP indemnity; push back: limited to gross negligence/willful misconduct.
- SLA & credits: customer asks for 99.99% for hosted API. Check if Dedicated offering can meet this; otherwise propose 99.9% with service credits capped per month. Add clear exclusion list (scheduled maintenance, force majeure, DDoS).
- Subprocessors / subcontracting: customer wants prior notice and approval for all subprocessors. We usually provide list and 30-day notice for changes. Proposed compromise: notice + objection window + only for material changes.
- Audit rights: customer requests on-site audit. Offer SOC2 report + encrypted logs export; restrict on-site audits to material breach with notice and cost allocation.
- Data deletion & retention: require 30-day data purge on termination. Confirm backend retention (backups) — propose retention <= 90 days for backups.
- Export controls & sanctions: add standard export control language; customer asked for US-only vendor operations — not acceptable for us.
- Model outputs & IP ownership: customer wants ownership of outputs. We can grant a license to use outputs but avoid transfer of model IP. Proposed language: customer owns customer-provided data and derivative outputs, vendor retains model IP.

Negotiation talking points (short)
- Training on customer data: "We will not use customer data to train or improve our base models. We may use de-identified telemetry to improve service reliability unless customer opts out."
- Liability cap: "Liability limited to the greater of aggregate fees paid in prior 12 months or $250,000 for security incidents; unlimited for willful misconduct/fraud."
- SLA: "99.9% uptime (monthly), credits up to X% of monthly invoice; exclusions: scheduled maintenance (48h notice), force majeure, customer misconfiguration."
- IP: "Customer retains rights to Customer Data and Outputs. Vendor retains all rights in models, model weights, and platform."
- Subprocessors: "Vendor will maintain a current list of subprocessors and provide notice of material changes; customer may raise objections within 30 days."

Redline snippets to consider (copy/paste candidates)
- Data training opt-out: "Vendor will not train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve its underlying models using Customer Data without Customer's prior written consent."
- Backup retention: "Vendor will delete Customer Data from production systems within 30 days of termination and from backups within 90 days, unless retention required by law."
- Audit: "Vendor will provide SOC2 Type II report upon request. On-site audits are permitted only in the event of a suspected material breach, with reasonable notice and cost-sharing."

Open questions / TODOs
- Confirm whether Dedicated placement in eu-west-1 with KMS satisfies customer's residency + key control ask (ask Infra/Private deploy team).
- Get copy of customer's standard DPA (J), compare against our DPA (Maya to own).
- Decide on dollar cap for security incidents for mid-market: propose $250k floor? (Finance input).
- Confirm whether we can support 99.99% SLA on Dedicated with existing infra (SRE/hosting).

Meeting prep (for negotiation call)
- Objectives: keep training prohibition, limit liability to fees x12, accept reasonable SLA with clear exclusions, offer SOC2 + on-demand logs, provide KMS option for keys.
- Ask: what controllers/processors do they have? any regulatory constraints (HIPAA, GLBA)?
- Leave-behind: two options: (1) Hosted with 99.9% + SOC2 + DPA + KMS (2) Dedicated + 99.99% + higher fee + enterprise DPA.

References/links
- DPA template: https://confluence.redwood.company/display/LEGAL/DPA+Template
- Jira: JIRA-RED-4567 (customer-contract-redlines)
- Internal convo: slack #legal-sales -> thread link (see Jira ticket for permalink)

Notes to self:
- Keep language as narrow as possible. Where customer wants broad rights (IP/indemnity), propose carveouts/exceptions.
- Flag any redline that could set precedence for other mid-market deals (esp liability & training).
- Run final language by Maya before sharing counters.

---
Last updated quick log:
- 2025-11-12: initial notes after receiving redline
- 2025-11-20: added SLA/backup retention thoughts
- 2026-02-20: updated with negotiation talking points and TODOs (after sync with Sales)

End of scratchpad.
